sources.entry: django-oauth-toolkit - An OAuth 2.0 authorization server for Django.

summary.one_liner: Django OAuth Toolkit is an OAuth 2.0 authorization server and resource server add-on for existing Django projects.
summary.what_it_does: Adds OAuth2 token issuing and management to a Django project through included endpoints, models, and logic, instead of running a separate auth service. Per the README, it can act as an authorization server, issuing and managing OAuth2 tokens. It can also act as a resource server to protect Django or Django REST Framework APIs with OAuth2. The README says it uses OAuthLib so the behavior is RFC-compliant. As of 3.4.0, the README says it supports the authorization server role for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) authorization spec, with PKCE required by default, RFC 8414 and RFC 9728 metadata endpoints in the default URLconf, and Dynamic Client Registration and Client ID Metadata Documents behind the DCR_ENABLED and CIMD_ENABLED settings.
use_cases: Issue OAuth2 tokens from an existing Django app
Protect Django or Django REST Framework APIs with OAuth2
Act as an OAuth2 provider instead of running a separate auth service
Support MCP authorization server requirements with PKCE
Enable dynamic client registration for OAuth clients
how_to_run: Add path('o/', include(oauth2_urls)) to urls.py, importing urls from oauth2_provider
notable: Built on OAuthLib for RFC-compliant OAuth2 behavior
Runs inside an existing Django project rather than as a separate service
PKCE required by default and RFC 8414/9728 discovery endpoints in 3.4.0
Optional Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591/7592) and Client ID Metadata Documents
caveats: README lists gaps in the MCP and DCR/CIMD support, pointing to a release discussion for details
README asks for help maintaining the project and says maintainers are needed
